A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Prism research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, latency and memory measurements, spectral-energy analysis, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds PBS-Attn comparisons and HunyuanVideo generation results, including Table 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: v2 adds an axis-wise adaptation for HunyuanVideo's 3D-RoPE, selecting high- and low-frequency dimensions separately within temporal, height, and width subspaces (Appendix D.2). The original dual-band scoring, temperature calibration, and mask union remain unchanged. Figure 10's identifier corrections clarify the existing Top-P procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds video generation with HunyuanVideo using VBench prompts, extending evaluation from language and video understanding to generating dense video outputs with 3D positional structure. The original PG19, LongBench, RULER, VideoMME, and LongVideoBench coverage is retained.

E2.justification: PBS-Attn, previously discussed only as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7. The existing comparators remain. SpargeAttention is still excluded; v2 adds an explanation for that exclusion.

E3.justification: The new generation experiment introduces output-fidelity evaluation against full attention using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, together with end-to-end speedup. Table 4 evaluates two XAttention thresholds and four Prism thresholds. This is a distinct evaluation protocol; the previously documented language and video-understanding protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a video-generation fidelity–speed trade-off across sparsity thresholds, and Appendix E adds a same-prompt visual case study comparing generated frames and temporal consistency. The spectral-division, calibration, and block-size ablations are retained; the block-size study moves from Appendix D to F.

E5.justification: No new empirical run counts, seed information, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. The block-size timing plot retains its error bars (v1 Figure 11; v2 Figure 12). Appendix A.4's variance argument concerns theoretical residuals rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds PBS-Attn results throughout the existing comparisons and six generation configurations in Table 4; Prism at threshold 0.97 reports PSNR 23.5 and 1.37× speedup. Existing entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. Figures 6–7 also revise existing timings: for example, MInference's plotted 128K latency changes from approximately 106 to 114 ms.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 extends the constant-content analysis with a mean-plus-residual decomposition, a deterministic residual bound, and a conditional residual RMS estimate proportional to 1/sqrt(B). New Appendix B adds YaRN frequency equations and spectral-boundary analysis. These substantially extend the theoretical treatment while retaining the original attenuation derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about pooling-induced attenuation, training-free dual-band calibration, accuracy preservation, and approximately 5× acceleration. The 5.1× wording already appeared in v1's abstract and results; its expanded use does not establish a stronger core claim.

C2.justification: v2 explains why YaRN should preserve the relevant high-frequency attenuation and discusses weak correlation and adversarial alignment when semantic content varies within blocks. It also states that the LLM spectral configuration does not transfer directly to HunyuanVideo and interprets the new results as supporting applicability to dense prediction.

D1.justification: v2 documents HunyuanVideo's RoPE base, axis dimensions, and axis-specific band sizes; PBS-Attn's threshold and segment size; and YaRN interpolation constants. Figure 10 replaces undefined threshold/logits references with p/probs. These improve documentation, although generation prompt counts and detailed sampling settings remain unspecified. The repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: HunyuanVideo and VBench are newly cited. Appendix D.3 adds a substantive rationale for excluding SpargeAttention, positioning its quantization and block-skipping optimizations as complementary to Prism's estimator. The related-work narrative otherwise remains stable; most reference edits update metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized heading and wording edits, adds a generation-results paragraph and appendix subsections, updates cross-references, and corrects bibliography metadata. Section 3.4 is renamed to emphasize block selection. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds generation Table 4, qualitative Figure 11, and a YaRN summary table. Existing tables and Figures 5–7 gain PBS-Attn entries or series, and Table 3 changes from a wrapped display to full width. The block-size figure is relocated and renumbered 12; the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper through an additional relevant comparator, a distinct generation evaluation, conditional theoretical extensions, and corrected pseudocode. These improve validation and clarity without replacing the original contribution. The gains remain limited by incomplete generation-protocol reporting, unexplained revisions to timing plots, and the cross-term suppression assumption underlying the new residual RMS argument.
